transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, honestly, I'm just... I'm really struggling lately with how I look, specifically this one area on my face. I work as a cashier, you know, at the grocery store on 5th Street, and the fluorescent lights in there are just awful. They're so bright and they cast these weird shadows, and I just know they're highlighting this uneven spot I have right where my nose meets my cheek. It's like this little bump or irregularity, I don't even know how to describe it properly, but it's just... it's not right. 

I see it every time I look in the mirror before my shift, and then I'm just thinking about it the whole time I'm ringing people up. I feel like every customer who comes through my line, every time my manager walks by to check on things, that's the very first thing they're staring at. It's so distracting. And it's not just at work, either. If I take a selfie, or if my friends tag me in a photo on Instagram, I zoom in right on that spot, and it just looks so obvious to me. I've tried pointing it out to my mom and my best friend, Sarah, and they both swear they have no idea what I'm talking about. They say my skin looks fine, that I'm crazy for even worrying about it, but I know they're just being nice because they don't want to hurt my feelings. I mean, how could they not see it? It's right there in the middle of my face. It's just making me so self-conscious all the time, and I don't know how to stop fixating on it.
Have you seen a dermatologist or had this area of your face checked by a medical professional to rule out any actual skin condition or physical abnormality?

Well, no, I haven't actually gone to a doctor for it or anything. I mean, I thought about it a few times, like maybe looking up a dermatologist online or something? But honestly, I don't even know if they would do anything because it's not like it hurts or itches, you know? It's not a rash or a mole that's changing colors or something strictly medical like that. It's just... the actual texture and the way it's raised and uneven. 

So I feel like if I went to a regular skin doctor, they'd just look at me like I was totally wasting their time because they deal with, I don't know, skin cancer and severe acne and actual diseases. Plus, my insurance from the grocery store isn't really the best anyway—I'm technically part-time even though they schedule me for almost forty hours a week, so the copay alone would probably be a lot for me to swing right now on my budget. 

I did think about maybe seeing someone eventually, but for now I just end up trying to fix it myself with makeup. Which, honestly, is a whole other nightmare because half the time the concealer just sits on top of the uneven part and makes the shadow look even worse under those awful fluorescent lights I was telling you about. It just cakes up by the middle of my shift, and then I'm hiding in the employee bathroom trying to blend it out with my finger, and I just feel like I'm making it more red and obvious to everyone. So, yeah, no, I haven't had any professionals look at it yet. I just don't even know who I would go to for something like this without them thinking I'm just being vain, even though it's literally ruining my day.
How long have you been feeling this way about the area on your face? Has it been weeks, months, or longer?

Oh, wow, um... how long? Gosh, it feels like it's been forever, but if I really sit down and think about it... I guess it started being a real issue maybe like, six or seven months ago? Yeah, probably right around the end of summer. Because I remember I was still wearing my hair pulled back a lot because of the heat, and when my hair is up, there's absolutely nothing to distract from my face, you know? Like, no bangs or face-framing layers to kind of hide the sides of my nose or my cheeks. 

I remember one specific day, it was a Tuesday, because Tuesdays are always truck days at the store, so it was super chaotic. I was in the breakroom, and they have this mirror right by the time clock. I was clocking in, and the light hit me just... wrong. And I saw it. I mean, maybe it was always there and I just never noticed it before? Or maybe it just popped up overnight, I don't know. But ever since that exact moment, I haven't been able to unsee it. 

At first, it was just like, "Oh, that's weird," and I'd check it maybe once or twice a day. But then it became this whole... thing. Like, by Halloween, I was already spending an extra twenty minutes in the morning trying to cover it up before work. And then through Thanksgiving and Christmas, it just got worse and worse in my head. Especially with all the family photos during the holidays! Oh my gosh, my aunt was taking pictures on her iPad, and the camera quality on those things is just brutal. I spent the whole dinner worrying about what angle she was getting of my face. So yeah, it's definitely been months. Not years, I don't think, but long enough that it feels like it's just taken over my entire routine and my whole thought process every single day.
Do you find yourself worrying about other parts of your body the same way you worry about that spot on your face?

Um, no, not really. I mean, not like this. Like, obviously, I have days where I feel bloated or I think my hair looks flat, you know, normal stuff that I think every girl my age worries about, especially when you're on your feet all day in an ugly polyester uniform shirt that doesn't flatter anyone. I mean, they make us wear these bright red polo shirts, and they are just the most unforgiving material, and sometimes I look in the mirror and think, "Ugh, my arms look weird in this," or "I wish my stomach was flatter." But it's fleeting, you know? It's not like... it's not like the spot on my face. 

With the spot, it's just this constant, nagging thing. Like, if I think my arms look chubby in my uniform, I just kind of shrug it off and get to work, and I don't think about it again until maybe I take the shirt off at the end of the day. But my face... it's just always there. It's front and center. I can't hide it under a baggy sweater or change into a different pair of jeans. It's the first thing people see when I say, "Did you find everything okay today?" 

So, yeah, I guess I have normal insecurities, like maybe I wish my teeth were a little whiter or my eyelashes were longer, but I don't spend twenty minutes obsessing over my eyelashes in the employee bathroom, you know? I'm not zooming in on my arms in Instagram photos to see if someone can tell they're a little soft. It's really just this one specific, uneven, shadowy spot right next to my nose that completely ruins my day and takes up all my energy. Everything else is just... fine, I guess. Normal. But this one thing is just driving me absolutely crazy.
